# Framio

> Framio is a free, MIT-licensed design canvas for coding agents. It renders React and Tailwind designs from files in a developer's repository, with element selection, responsive viewports, and pinned comments.

Framio works with Claude Code, Codex, and other agents that read `.claude/skills` or `.agents/skills`, such as OpenCode, Cursor, Grok CLI, and Antigravity. Your agent writes each screen as a React and Tailwind file, and you click elements or pin comments on the canvas to tell it what to fix. Because Framio runs inside the agent's session in the repository, the agent reads the existing code, theme, and copy before designing. It can redesign an existing page (it screenshots the running app onto a moodboard and derives DESIGN.md from the current product), design new pages that match an existing product, and build a chosen design into the app, comparing app screenshots with the design at every width. The canvas runs on your own computer or VM. Measured with v0.0.7 on an Apple M4: framio start serves the canvas in about 0.6 seconds, a saved frame rebuilds in about 100 milliseconds, and the macOS download is 33 MB. It supports macOS on Apple Silicon and Linux x64 and arm64. It does not include a coding agent or model subscription.

## New in v0.0.8

`framio start` listens on all IPv4 interfaces by default and prints local, network, and available Tailscale URLs. SSH into a VM, start Framio in the repo, and open a printed URL on your main computer. Tailscale must be running to advertise its URL. Use `framio start --host 127.0.0.1` for local-only access. Anyone who can reach the port can edit the canvas, so limit access to a trusted network with firewall and Tailscale rules. Tailscale encrypts traffic through its tunnel. HTTPS needs a separate setup such as Tailscale Serve.

The VM does not need a desktop browser or display. SSH, CI, and headless Linux sessions skip automatic browser launch. Live previews work without Chromium. Screenshots, thumbnails, and geometry inspection need Framio's headless Chromium, its system libraries, and sandbox support. Remote HTTP clipboard actions are supported.

The canvas and CLI share update downloads, progress, and installation state. Use the canvas update control or `framio upgrade --check`, `--download`, and `--install`. Downloads are checksum-verified. Restart a running project to use the installed version. `framio upgrade --rollback` restores the previous binary. Binary updates do not update project skills, dependencies, themes, or designs. Older releases without `framio upgrade` can use the installer to get v0.0.8 or later.

Framio is an independent open-source project. It is not affiliated with Frame.io, Adobe's video review platform.
